Introduction and meaning
Fabricating false evidence. Historical concordance: IPC 192. For conduct governed by the BNS, cite BNS section 228; the IPC reference is historical concordance.
In student language: BNS s. 228 is the rule on “Fabricating false evidence”. The section provides that whoever causes any circumstance to exist or makes any false entry in any book or record, or electronic record or makes any document or electronic record containing a false statement, intending that such circumstance, false entry or false statement may appear in evidence in a judicial proceeding, or in a proceeding taken by law before a public servant as such, or before an arbitrator, and that such circumstance, false entry or false statement, so appearing in evidence, may cause any person who in such proceeding is to form an opinion upon the evidence, to entertain an erroneous opinion touching any point material to the result of such proceeding is said “to fabricate false evidence”. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 228 exists so that “Fabricating false evidence” has a closed legal test in Chapter XIV — Of False Evidence and Offences Against Public Justice. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Perjury, screening, harbouring, false charge, and failing to appear on a bond.

The provision in detail
228. Whoever causes any circumstance to exist or makes any false entry in any book or record, or electronic record or makes any document or electronic record containing a false statement, intending that such circumstance, false entry or false statement may appear in evidence in a judicial proceeding, or in a proceeding taken by law before a public servant as such, or before an arbitrator, and that such circumstance, false entry or false statement, so appearing in evidence, may cause any person who in such proceeding is to form an opinion upon the evidence, to entertain an erroneous opinion touching any point material to the result of such proceeding is said “to fabricate false evidence”

Essential ingredients
1. Whoever causes any circumstance to exist or makes any false entry in any book or record, or electronic record or makes any document or electronic record containing a false statement, intending that such circumstance, false entry or false statement may appear in evidence in a judicial proceeding, or in a proceeding taken by law before a public servant as such, or before an arbitrator, and that such circumstance, false entry or false statement, so appearing in evidence, may cause any person who in such proceeding is to form an opinion upon the evidence, to entertain an erroneous opinion touching any point material to the result of such proceeding is said “to fabricate false evidence”

Statutory illustrations
Illustration (a). A puts jewels into a box belonging to Z, with the intention that they may be found in that box, and that this circumstance may cause Z to be convicted of theft. A has fabricated false evidence

Exam use: quote illustration (a), then write which ingredient of BNS s. 228 it proves. Copying the illustration without that mapping sentence does not score.

Illustration (b). A makes a false entry in his shop-book for the purpose of using it as corroborative evidence in a Court. A has fabricated false evidence

Exam use: quote illustration (b), then write which ingredient of BNS s. 228 it proves. Copying the illustration without that mapping sentence does not score.

Illustration (c). A, with the intention of causing Z to be convicted of a criminal conspiracy, writes a letter in imitation of Z’s handwriting, purporting to be addressed to an accomplice in such criminal conspiracy, and puts the letter in a place which he knows that the officers of the police are likely to search. A has fabricated false evidence

Exam use: quote illustration (c), then write which ingredient of BNS s. 228 it proves. Copying the illustration without that mapping sentence does not score.

hypotheticals.question: Whether BNS s. 228 (Fabricating false evidence) applies, and how structured written arguments should be framed.
hypotheticals.analysis:
Step 1 — Identify the provision. The correct current-law cite is BNS s. 228 (Fabricating false evidence), Chapter XIV — Of False Evidence and Offences Against Public Justice.
Step 2 — State the legal test in your own words, then list the ingredients:
   (1) Whoever causes any circumstance to exist or makes any false entry in any book or record, or electronic record or makes any document or electronic record containing a false statement, intending that such circumstance, false entry or false statement may appear in evidence in a judicial proceeding, or in a proceeding taken by law before a public servant as such, or before an arbitrator, and that such circumstance, false entry or false statement, so appearing in evidence, may cause any person who in such proceeding is to form an opinion upon the evidence, to entertain an erroneous opinion touching any point material to the result of such proceeding is said “to fabricate false evidence”
Step 3 — Check limitations, provisos and the rest of the Chapter so you do not apply s. 228 in a vacuum.
Step 4 — Map each fact to an ingredient. Write “this fact proves ingredient (a)” or “this fact is missing, so the section is not made out”.
Step 5 — Conclude. If every essential ingredient is proved and no exception covers the case, BNS s. 228 applies. If any essential ingredient fails, say so and stop. Do not invent a different section to save the answer.

Core Legal Mandate: Whoever causes any circumstance to exist or makes any false entry in any book or record, or electronic record or makes any document or electronic record containing a false statement, intending that su...
Classification and Sentencing: Structured under Chapter XIV penal tiers.
Evidentiary and Procedural Cognate: Governed by the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 and Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.
essentialIngredients: The commission of an act or omission falling within the statutory description of Fabricating false evidence.
The existence of the requisite culpable mental state (intention, knowledge, rashness, or negligence) prescribed under Section 228.
The absence of any statutory justification, exception, or lawful authority under Chapter III (General Exceptions).
The resulting consequence or endangerment specified in the statutory formula of Section 228.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 228 constitutes a key component of Chapter XIV (Of False Evidence and Offences against Public Justice) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, addressing fabricating false evidence. The provision balances personal liberty with public interest and social order. The prosecution must establish every statutory element beyond reasonable doubt: the specified actus reus, the requisite mens rea, and any relevant statutory circumstances. Modern judicial interpretation emphasizes substantive fairness, proportionality in sentencing, and adherence to constitutional safeguards. Where statutory exceptions or provisos are attached to the section, the accused must establish facts bringing the case within such provisions under evidentiary standards.
examples: Teaching example (Standard application): An individual intentionally commits acts satisfying the statutory formula of fabricating false evidence under Section 228 without lawful authority. The individual is liable under BNS s. 228.

Teaching example (Absence of mens rea / Lawful exception): A person acts in good faith or without the requisite statutory mental element under circumstances recognized by law. The essential ingredients of Section 228 are not satisfied; no penal liability attaches.
distinctions: Section 228 vs General Attempt: Section 228 penalizes the substantive conduct specified in Chapter XIV; inchoate attempts without specific provisions fall under the general attempt provisions.

Section 228 vs Cognate Chapter Offences: Liability under Section 228 is distinguished by its specific mental threshold and the particular legal interest protected under Of False Evidence and Offences against Public Justice.
problemApplication: Issue: Whether the accused is liable under BNS s. 228 for conduct relating to fabricating false evidence.
Rule: Under BNS s. 228, liability attaches upon proof of the statutory actus reus accompanied by the requisite mens rea without lawful justification.
Application: The evidence demonstrates that the accused performed the specified act with the required state of mind, satisfying all statutory ingredients of Section 228.
Conclusion: The accused is guilty of an offence under BNS s. 228 and subject to the prescribed punishment.
